findings.title: Failed result processing is still marked complete
findings.body: The `finally` block marks every work item complete, including items whose processor raised an exception. `ResultProcessor.__call__` also catches and suppresses exceptions from `handle_result`, so those failures appear successful to this worker. The commit loop can therefore advance past a result that was never processed, preventing Kafka from replaying it and causing data loss.

findings.title: Unseen Kafka offsets can permanently block commits
findings.body: This loop requires every integer offset between the first and last observed offsets to be present in `all_offsets`. Kafka consumers can legitimately observe gaps, for example from compacted records or transactional control records. When that happens, processing later messages will never make the missing offset appear, so commits remain stuck at the gap and the consumer can accumulate an unbounded backlog.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure
findings.body: `queue.Queue()` defaults to `maxsize=0`, which means unlimited capacity. If messages arrive faster than workers process them, the consumer continues enqueueing work instead of slowing ingestion; queued payloads can grow until the process runs out of memory. This also contradicts the strategy's stated backpressure guarantee.

findings.title: Closing one strategy permanently shuts down the shared worker pool
findings.body: The queue pool is created once on `ResultsStrategyFactory` and reused by every strategy returned from `create_with_partitions`, but closing any one strategy shuts that shared pool down. Arroyo can create and close strategies again when partitions are reassigned; the replacement strategy then submits to queues whose workers have exited (or which reject submissions), so processing stops after a rebalance.

findings.title: A negative worker count creates a zero-queue pool
findings.body: `max_workers` is passed directly as `num_queues` when it is negative. The pool then creates no queues, and processing a message fails during `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`; `submit` catches that error and marks the message's offset complete, allowing it to be committed without processing. Validate that the configured worker count is positive before starting the consumer.
